about: MUTATING — set Longhorn's ONE setting node-drain-policy (infra/forge/longhorn-drain-policy.sh <value> <plan_sha256>) through the forge's ops_kubectl door (the admin kubeconfig David placed, infra/estate/ops-credentials.sh). Asked for by David 2026-09-30 ~05:05Z, option (a) for the w-1 NVMe window (backlog 46584350; backlog 52ea56ac, review 8599a3a8 M1/M2): rather than copy /work or gate-runner-disk onto a control plane beside etcd — w-1 is the only talos-worker — relax the policy for the window (allow-if-replica-is-stopped) and set it back after w-1 boots; the NVMe is ADDED and w-1's own disk stays, so a one-replica volume survives the power-off, and the drain is held only by the default block-if-contains-last-replica. Both directions are this verb. AUTHORISED PER RUN BY DAVID'S PASSKEY in design 17835005's shape, as set-volume-replicas and shutdown-node are: it declares requires_approval with the read-only plan-a-longhorn-drain-policy (this script's --plan) as its plan_verb, so the runner renders the plan onto the request's approve step, runs this only after a passkey on the approvers list signs those bytes, and hands the script sha256 of the SIGNED plan; the script re-renders and patches nothing unless today's plan hashes to it. The value before is in the bytes and a plan that changes nothing is refused, so a second run of an applied plan is refused: at most once. THE BOUND IS THE SCRIPT'S, NEVER A PARAM: the setting is fixed (no argument names one); the value must be one of the options Longhorn's LIVE definition enumerates, read from its manager API, never retyped here; the definition must not be read-only; and the stored setting and Longhorn's API must agree on the value that stands — or nothing is done (exit 78). THE WRITE is one kubectl patch --type=json that TESTS `value` is still the planned one and replaces it — a compare-and-set on the one field, judged again by Longhorn's admission webhook. THE EFFECT IS READ BACK: every 5 s for up to 90 s, the stored setting and Longhorn's API; only when both read the new value and the API reports it applied is the effect line printed, and otherwise the run exits 1 saying it is NOT proven, naming what each read. Timeout 180: the reads (20-30 s each at worst), the patch, and the script's own 90 s read-back, which gives its verdict before the runner's kill. A non-default value does not stay forgotten: check-longhorn-drain-policy reads it every day and its watch files an urgent alarm once it has stood 24 hours.
effect: ^set-longhorn-drain-policy: node-drain-policy reads back [a-z-]+ — settings\.longhorn\.io value [a-z-]+, Longhorn's API value [a-z-]+, applied true \(was [a-z-]+; Longhorn's default [a-z-]+; after [0-9]+s\)$
